questions.q: Four functions each write { amount: number } inline in their signatures. A currency field is later added to the objects. Why does nothing fail to compile?
questions.explain: With one named Money type used everywhere, adding currency to it makes every place that builds money without a currency fail to compile, which is exactly where decisions must be made.
options: Because TypeScript ignores extra properties everywhere
Because each function has its own private idea of the shape; nothing connects them, so none of them is told the concept changed
Because inline types are erased earlier than named ones

questions.q: Which of these can only be named with type, not with interface?
questions.explain: An interface can only describe an object type. Unions, tuples, primitives and computed types need a type alias.
options: An object with a method deposit(amount: number): void
The public shape of a class

questions.q: Given type Naira = number and type Kobo = number, what happens when you pass a Kobo value to a parameter of type Naira?
questions.explain: An alias is a name, not a new type. To make units truly distinct you need branded types; until then, use one unit everywhere and name variables clearly (feeKobo).
options: Error: Kobo is not assignable to Naira
Nothing: both aliases mean number, so the compiler sees no difference
The value is converted from kobo to naira automatically

questions.q: Which declaration is valid?
questions.explain: An interface can extend several parents, and they may be interfaces or aliases of object types. A type alias combines with & instead of extends, and nothing can extend a union.
options: interface Savings extends Account, InterestTerms { … }, where InterestTerms is an object type alias

questions.q: interface Account { id: string } and interface Legacy extends Account { id: number }. Where is the error reported?
questions.explain: extends checks that the child is compatible with the parent right at the declaration, and explains which property clashes.
options: Nowhere; the child's id overrides the parent's
Only when a Legacy value is created

questions.q: What is the type of id in type Legacy = Account & { id: number }, where Account has id: string?
questions.explain: string & number is empty. The intersection is accepted, and the problem only appears later, when someone tries to create a value. That is the practical reason to prefer extends for object hierarchies.
options: never, and the declaration itself compiles without an error
A compile error on the declaration

questions.q: You really do need a legacy account whose id is a number. How should you declare it?
questions.explain: Omit removes the old id first, so the new one does not conflict. The first option is TS2430, the second silently makes id never, and any throws away checking.

questions.q: A module declares interface Transfer { from: string; to: string } and, much further down, interface Transfer { reference: string }. What happens?
questions.explain: That is declaration merging. It is silent where it happens; the error shows up wherever a Transfer without a reference is written.
options: The second declaration replaces the first
They merge into one interface requiring from, to and reference, with no error at either declaration
The first declaration wins and the second is ignored

questions.q: What happens if a module declares type Fee = { amount: number } twice?
questions.explain: Type aliases never merge. A duplicate name is reported where it is written, which is often what you want.
options: Error TS2300 "Duplicate identifier 'Fee'" on both declarations
Nothing, if the shapes are the same

questions.q: What is module augmentation for?
questions.explain: declare module "./events.js" { interface TransferEvent { riskScore?: number } } reopens that module's scope, and the interface merges with the original. Plugin systems rely on this.
options: Making every interface in a project optional
Adding fields to an interface declared in another module you do not own, such as a library's or a core module's type that a plugin decorates

questions.q: Why should a plugin's augmentation add riskScore?: number rather than riskScore: number?
questions.explain: Merging changes the type for everybody. Only the plugin sets the score, so only the plugin should be able to assume it is there.
options: A required field becomes required on every TransferEvent in the whole program, including code that has never heard of the plugin

questions.q: Why can two files that both declare interface Account merge in an old-style project, but not in the course's setup?
questions.explain: Merging only happens within a scope. With "type": "module" and module: "NodeNext", each file is a module, so accidental cross-file merging cannot happen.
options: Files without imports or exports are scripts sharing one global scope, where same-named interfaces merge; every file in the course's setup is a module with its own scope
Because interfaces in .ts files are private

questions.q: Which type correctly describes a chart of accounts where each account can contain sub-accounts?
questions.explain: The self-reference goes through an array, so a leaf account simply has an empty list. The first option requires infinitely many nested accounts, the third refers to itself directly (an error), and the fourth throws away checking.
options: interface LedgerAccount { name: string; children: readonly LedgerAccount[] }

questions.q: In totalBalance(account) = account.children.reduce((sum, c) => sum + totalBalance(c), account.balance), what is the base case?
questions.explain: The data shape provides the base case. Leaves have children: [], and the recursion stops there.
options: There is none, so it recurses forever
An account with no children: reduce over an empty array returns the starting value, the account's own balance
An account with a zero balance

questions.q: Why is type Json = string | number | boolean | null | Json[] | { [key: string]: Json } a better type for parsed JSON than any?
questions.explain: Like every type, it is erased, so it does not validate. But unlike any, it does not switch checking off: you must narrow before calling string or array methods.
options: It validates the JSON at runtime
It says exactly what JSON can contain and still forces you to check which kind of value you have before using it

questions.q: A value typed with an interface is refused by a function that takes Record<string, string>, although every property is a string. Why?
questions.explain: The error is TS2345, "Index signature for type 'string' is missing in type …". Spreading into a fresh object or giving the function a more specific parameter type fixes it.
options: An interface could be merged with more members later, so TypeScript will not assume it has an implicit index signature; a type alias is closed and can be checked
It is a bug in TypeScript 7

questions.q: interface Customer { name: string; phone: string } and type Contact = { name: string; phone: string }. Can a Customer be passed where a Contact is expected?
questions.explain: Whether a type was declared with type or interface does not change compatibility between plain object shapes. (The index-signature rule is the exception.)
options: Yes: TypeScript compares shapes, not names (structural typing)

questions.q: Which signature lets the SMS function serve both customers and staff?
questions.explain: Ask for the smallest type the function needs. The intersection would require a value that is both a customer and a staff member at once.
options: smsLine(contact: ContactDetails, text: string), where both types extend ContactDetails

questions.q: Which choice follows the convention "interface for object shapes, type for everything else"?
questions.explain: Object shapes (especially ones others extend or augment) as interfaces; unions, tuples and function types as aliases. The first option is not valid syntax.
options: type TransferServiceOptions = { retries: number; timeoutMs: number } only because aliases are faster

questions.q: Why should a request context type that plugins add fields to be an interface?
questions.explain: A plugin can reopen the module and add fields to an interface. A type alias cannot be reopened; a second declaration is a duplicate-identifier error.
options: Because interfaces are faster at runtime
Because only interfaces can be augmented through declaration merging
Because type aliases cannot have string properties
Because interfaces are validated at runtime

questions.q: ZudoJS's conventions ask for interface names without an I prefix (EventBus, not IEventBus). What is a good reason?
questions.explain: If IEventBus later becomes a type alias or a class, every import would need renaming. A domain name stays correct.
options: Callers depend on the concept, not on whether it was declared with interface or type; the prefix leaks a detail that may change
The prefix makes the type slower
Interfaces must start with a lowercase letter

questions.q: A Customer with kycLevel: 1 | 2 | 3 is loaded from a database row. What guarantees that kycLevel is really 1, 2 or 3?
questions.explain: Types are erased. A row with kycLevel = 7 becomes a "Customer" with 7 unless code checks it when it enters the program.
options: The interface, because it is readonly
Only a runtime check (and ideally a database constraint); the interface only describes what you expect

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Both aliases are number, so the kobo value (₦25) is added as ₦2,500. The compiler cannot tell the units apart.
options: It does not compile: Kobo is not Naira

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Every Savings is also an Account, so label accepts it. 6% of 500000 is 30000.
options: It does not compile: label needs an Account

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Each node adds its own balance to the totals of its children: ATMs is 2500 + 300 = 2800, and Cash is 100 + 4000 + 2800 = 6900.

questions.q: Interfaces are erased. What does this print?
questions.explain: The two declarations merge, so the object must have both properties. At runtime there is no interface at all: r is a plain object with two keys.
options: It does not compile: duplicate identifier

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: A plain value has depth 0. The array adds 1. The object adds 1, its entries array adds 1, and the inner object adds 1: 3.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Passing ada directly would be refused, because it is typed with an interface. The spread creates a fresh object literal type, which TypeScript can check against the index signature.
options: It does not compile: index signature is missing

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The function type alias gives both arrow functions their parameter type. 250,000 kobo is ₦2,500 (fine); 9,000,000 kobo is ₦90,000, over the 5,000,000-kobo limit. Underscores in numbers are only for readability.
options: must be positive | over the ₦50,000 limit

questions.q: A plugin augmented TransferEvent with an optional riskScore. What does this print?
questions.explain: The merged interface has an optional riskScore, so the first event is valid without one. ?? replaces the missing value.
options: It does not compile: riskScore is missing

questions.q: Define an interface Money with kobo: number and currency: "NGN" | "USD". Write total(items: Money[]): Money that throws Error("mixed currencies") when currencies differ. Print the two lines shown.
questions.explain: Because the return type is Money, the function cannot forget the currency, and has to decide what a mixed total means. Here it refuses.

questions.q: Create ContactDetails (name, phone), and Customer and StaffMember interfaces that extend it (with customerId and branch). Write smsLine(contact: ContactDetails, text: string) and print one line for each.
questions.explain: smsLine asks only for the contact details, so both entity types fit. Neither has to pretend to be the other.
questions.expected:
to 0803 000 1111 (Ada): Statement ready
to 0805 222 3333 (Tunde): Shift starts at 8

questions.q: Write a recursive Note interface (author, replies) and countNotes(note) that counts the note and every reply at any depth. Print 4.
questions.explain: The type refers to itself through the replies array, and the function mirrors it: count this note, plus everything under each reply. A note with no replies is the base case.

questions.q: Declare LegacyAccount so that it has every property of Account except that id is a number, using extends and Omit. Print 42 Ada.
questions.explain: Omit<Account, "id"> is Account without id, so the new id: number does not clash. Without Omit, extends reports TS2430, and & would make id never.

questions.q: Write interfaces Deposit (kind: "deposit", kobo) and Withdrawal (kind: "withdrawal", kobo, atmId), a type Transaction union of both, and balance(history). Print 12000 for a deposit of 15000 and a withdrawal of 3000.
questions.explain: Each member is an interface; the union needs a type alias, because only an alias can name a union.

questions.q: The function below demands a whole Customer, so it cannot be used for staff. Change only its parameter type to the smallest shape it needs, so both calls compile and print.
questions.explain: The function only reads name and email. Asking for exactly that lets any object with those two properties in, thanks to structural typing. In a real codebase, give that shape a name such as ContactDetails.

questions.q: Write print(account, depth) for a recursive LedgerAccount (code, name, children) that prints each account indented by two spaces per level.
questions.explain: The default parameter depth = 0 lets the first call leave it out; each recursive call passes depth + 1 for the next level down.

questions.q: A plugin file contains declare module "./events.js" { interface TransferEvent { riskScore?: number } }, but main.ts reports that riskScore does not exist. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explain: An augmentation only applies when the file that declares it is part of the program. Importing the plugin (as main.ts does with fraud.ts in the lesson) brings it in.
options: Module augmentation only works for type aliases
The plugin file is not part of the compilation, for example because nothing imports it, so the augmentation is never seen
Optional properties cannot be added by augmentation
The module path must not have a file extension

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Both values have a city string, so both fit Location, whether their own type came from a type, an interface or inference. Extra properties are fine when passing a variable (the excess-property check only applies to object literals written in place).
options: It does not compile: Branch is not a Location

questions.q: Write a type alias FxRate for a labelled tuple [from: Currency, to: Currency, rate: number], where type Currency = "NGN" | "USD" | "GBP", and convert(amount, from, to, rates) that returns the converted amount rounded to a whole number. Print 62000 for $40 to naira.
questions.explain: A tuple can only be named with a type alias. The labels (from, to, rate) are documentation; the positions and their types are what the compiler checks.
